//: Declared merge-policy target state across the active Goldberry-Playground repos (GOL-1819).
//gate: Ruleset and branch-protection WRITES are board-gated and not agent-executable (same class as GOL-392 / GOL-1207). scripts/ci/apply-merge-policy.sh --check is safe for anyone; --apply is Josh-only and needs an admin token. This file is the single source of truth so future drift is a diff, not archaeology.
//systems: GitHub unions two policy systems. 'ruleset' repos carry the settings in their named repository ruleset; 'legacy' repos carry them in classic branch protection on 'branch'. The script maps the canonical target keys below to the right API surface per system.
//fields: Canonical target keys (a key that is absent for a repo is NOT managed there): strict = require branch up-to-date with base (ruleset required_status_checks.strict_required_status_checks_policy | legacy required_status_checks.strict); dismiss_stale_reviews = dismiss approvals on push (ruleset pull_request.dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push | legacy required_pull_request_reviews.dismiss_stale_reviews); thread_resolution = require all review threads resolved (ruleset pull_request.required_review_thread_resolution | legacy required_conversation_resolution); extra_approval_unattributed = require a second approval for unattributed commits (ruleset pull_request.require_extra_approval_for_unattributed_changes | legacy: n/a).
//required_contexts: GOL-1953: the full required status-check context set for the branch (ruleset required_status_checks.required_status_checks[] | legacy required_status_checks.checks[]). This is the DECLARED TARGET — the guard layer (protected-paths / config-freeze / fix-touches-test / CI scripts / required-checks-audit + per-repo security checks) is promoted from advisory to branch-binding here. EVERY listed context was verified to report success on an actual merge_group commit first (acceptance #1) — a context whose job is skipped/conditional on merge_group (e.g. AgenticOS 'Dependency review', gated by a pull_request-only preflight) is DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED because it would wedge the merge queue. On --apply, legacy new contexts inherit the app_id shared by existing checks (15368 = GitHub Actions) and existing pins are preserved (never loosened); ruleset entries preserve any integration_id. LOCKSTEP: this list must equal the same repo's .github/required-checks.json (GOL-1907's reconcile leg hard-fails on declared-vs-live drift). Apply a repo (`--apply --repo X`) in the same batch as that repo's required-checks.json bump so a weekly reconcile never sees a mismatch. For a repo whose promotion PR has not landed yet, --check will show this as pending drift — expected, not a failure.
//out-of-scope: Not changed by this policy: required_approving_review_count and the merge-queue rulesets themselves.
